text:
morgan: quick heads-up, ran into a customer bug where our async client retries after a 5xx while the auth hook refreshes the token, and the retry arrives without the Idempotency-Key. duplicate resource created.
lee: wow. do you have a short repro?
morgan: yep, fairly small. gist: client has auth callback that does `await maybe_refresh()` and returns headers. first request 502s, retry happens, but server sees no Idempotency-Key on retry.
morgan: minimal snippet below:
```python
async def create_order(client):
    hdrs = {"Idempotency-Key": str(uuid4())}
    await client.post("/orders", json={"sku": "X"}, headers=hdrs)
# auth callback may replace header dict during refresh
```
anita: is the auth callback mutating a shared headers dict or returning a new one? that pattern matters with async retries.
sam: looked at transport: on replay we rebuild the request but copy `req.headers` by reference. if auth replaces the headers container between attempt 1 and 2, the reconstructed request may end up with a different dict that lacks the idempotency key. also race if headers mutated concurrently.
lee: so two root causes: (1) unsafe header sharing/mutation in user auth hook, (2) our retry reconstitution doesn't guarantee preserving per-attempt ephemeral headers.
morgan: customer impact = duplicate billing. happened when token TTL was ~short and load was high.
anita: immediate mitigations: (A) server-side: add dedupe logic where possible (not always feasible), (B) client-side: treat headers as immutable per attempt — deep-copy headers at send time and stash original idempotency key to re-insert on retries. also document anti-patterns.
sam: quick patch idea: in async_transport.send_attempt do `attempt_headers = dict(req.headers)` at attempt start, and on retry if `Idempotency-Key` missing but `req._first_idempotency` exists, restore it. will add unit test that simulates auth hook swapping the headers dict.
lee: also emit metric `client.retry.idempotency_restored` so we can find customers hit by this in the wild.
ci-bot: created issue #2981: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2981 (py-async-auth-header-swap-replay) by sam
morgan: adding to monday triage. sam to own patch and add flaky repro case.
sam: will open PR with tests and a short auth guide note: avoid sharing mutable header containers across coroutines; prefer returning a fresh dict or using a callback that applies auth to a copy.
anita: also add a short example in docs showing safe auth callback pattern.
lee: thanks team. once PR lands, we'll validate with customer repro and roll out. :rocket:
